q: Under what statistical properties of the trained weight matrices W_n does the paper's within-run |analytic - MC| <= 0.05 at beta=1.5 hold? On our independently trained L=5 network the same-measure deviation is 15-56x worse (max |Delta| = 0.888).
basis: We reproduced the exact analytic formulas (Eqs. 37/41/42) with 6+ order-of-magnitude mean accuracy at beta=0.1, so the implementation is correct. Yet at beta=1.5 our correlation deviations vs 100k-sample MC are max 0.888 / mean 0.382 vs the paper's max 0.05 / mean 0.016 on the SAME 10-pair set.
next_steps: Systematic sweep: for many independently seeded 5-layer nets trained to matched nRMSE, compute the flip-set fraction ||1|| / N per layer as a function of beta, and correlate against the analytic-vs-MC correlation-matrix RMSE. Look for a spectral norm ||W|| threshold or bias-magnitude condition that separates the tight from the loose regime.

q: Does the paper's claim that linearization error DECREASES with depth (Fig. 10) hold once train nRMSE is matched across depths? Our L=20 net (nRMSE=0.078, worse than L=5's 0.028) shows the OPPOSITE trend.
basis: At beta=0.1 our corr_offdiag_RMSE grows 0.031 (L=1) -> 0.060 (L=5) -> 0.937 (L=20). This contradicts Fig. 10 of the paper.
next_steps: Retrain L=20 with residual connections (paper's Appendix C ResNet) so that train nRMSE matches L=5, then re-measure the analytic-vs-MC agreement. Also do a paired-seed controlled experiment: train {L=1, L=5, L=20} nets until each hits the same held-out MSE, then compare corr RMSE.

q: How do the sinc-product Fourier PDF integrals (Eq. A.4) scale numerically as Nx grows? The integrand oscillates on scale 1/(beta q_min) and decays only as a^{-Nx}, and our truncation a_max = 40/(beta*min|q_jn|) is heuristic.
basis: We had to add a sign+log-abs treatment to avoid underflow in the product. On Nx=31 this works, but scaling to Nx=100 or 200 (finer GLL grids) is not obviously stable.
next_steps: Derive an a priori truncation error bound based on min|q_jn| and Nx, then benchmark against a direct 2^k-sample quasi-MC (Sobol) reference at increasing Nx. Also compare against a Fast-Fourier-based iterated-convolution implementation of Eq. (A.5) as suggested but not implemented in the paper.

q: All results assume z ~ U[-beta,beta]^Nx (uniform iid). What is the closed-form marginal PDF when z is correlated Gaussian, and does the linearization-improves-with-depth claim survive that change?
basis: The paper's moment formulas (Eqs. 37/41 with the covariance Q in Eq. 39) generalize immediately, but the sinc-product PDF (Eq. A.4) is derived specifically from the uniform box shape. Real forward-UQ applications (climate, PDE) almost always have correlated Gaussian inputs.
next_steps: Rederive Eq. (A.1) with p(z) = multivariate Gaussian: the inner integral becomes a Gaussian characteristic function exp(-1/2 a^2 q_j^T Sigma q_j), which gives a Gaussian marginal for g_j. Test whether Fig. 10's depth-monotonicity survives Gaussian z on the same operator.

q: How does the analytic-vs-MC agreement deteriorate as the operator's nonlinearity grows beyond the paper's mildly-quadratic (63)? For strongly nonlinear operators (e.g., PDE flow maps like Kuramoto-Sivashinsky), does the linearised-leaky-ReLU still recover variance to first order in beta or does it fail catastrophically?
basis: Even on (63), our L=5 network shows variance_median_rel_err growing from 2.1% at beta=0.1 to 47.5% at beta=1.5. Steeper nonlinearity in the target operator means larger effective Lipschitz constants of the trained network and more sign-flips per beta, which should sharpen the gap.
next_steps: Train MLP surrogates for a sequence of operators with tunable nonlinearity (e.g., g = int f + eps * f^k for k=1,2,3,5) and measure the analytic-vs-MC variance error as a function of both beta and k. Look for a phase-transition-like collapse.
